title: Align setup CPU presets with canonical config
summary: Keep setup-emitted VideoPreset values on the canonical descriptor registry, write libx265 speed choices only to CpuEncodePreset, and preserve integer types for setup-authored numeric fields.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W02-006. The safest no-GPU setup default wrote VideoPreset=medium even though the canonical schema, Python contract, and engine registry accept only p1-p7 for that key.
affected_areas: setup integer input and config emission
behavior_before: Selecting the CPU/libx265 profile or manually tuning its preset stored libx265 speed names in VideoPreset, and the setup-local compatibility helper contradicted the canonical contract by accepting those invalid values.
behavior_after: Setup profiles and prompts derive from the canonical registries, retain a p1-p7 VideoPreset for every codec, store CPU speed in CpuEncodePreset, default no-GPU first runs to the valid CPU profile, and emit integer-only setup fields with canonical integer types.
tests_added: Extend Invoke-ConfigKeyRegistryChecks.ps1 with no-GPU CPU-profile selection, canonical preset-key mapping, registry-derived manual choices, emitted PSD1 schema validation, and integer-reader type assertions.
manual_validation: Pre-fix Invoke-ConfigKeyRegistryChecks.ps1 - expected red because Get-SetupVideoProfiles did not exist; the first post-fix run then caught the OrderedDictionary copy defect before the IDictionary correction.

Focused Invoke-ConfigKeyRegistryChecks.ps1 - passed: 206 registered keys and references across 166 PowerShell files; exercised no-GPU CPU selection, canonical CPU/GPU preset registries, schema-valid CPU config emission, and integer input typing.

notes: Setup/config emission only. The packaged dry-run exposed that the setup numeric reader returned doubles for integer-only canonical fields; this packet fixes that required validation-path blocker by accepting and returning positive integers at every existing call site. It does not remediate the separate W02-010 zero/null validation finding. No engine command generation, encoder routing, source media, scratch, publish, or destination policy changes. Representative real media is not required.
